newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to restructure CEC savings bank.
newsitem.headline: Romania to restructure CEC savings bank.

text.p: The Romanian government on Friday said it had decided to restructure the state-owned Casa de Economii si Consemnatiuni SA (CEC) commercial bank, formerly a savings bank, and place it under central bank supervision.

"Our intention is to prevent any possible collapse, so we will put CEC under the central bank's control, instead of the state's supervision," Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara told a news conference at the end of a government meeting.
The new bill would prevent any "interference" by the finance ministry in the CEC's policy Ciumara said.
CEC deposits would be fully guaranteed by the state, Ciumara said.
Under the regulations, only deposits of up to 10 million are guaranteed.
"The CEC will remain a bank of very low risk but also with low interest rates," Ciumara said.

Romania's centrist government has recently promoted legislation to increase the supervision power and autonomy of the central bank, as part of its reform measures. The laws are still to be approved by the parliament.
